name: Florum
description: A Normandy Tribunal covenant in Ghent disguised as a suburb owned by the fictional de Spinnen family; it employs the Spinnen and leads support for the Lotharingian Tribunal.

name: De Spinnen Family
description: A fictional old farming family maintained by the magi of Florum as landlords and public face of the covenant.

name: Piet de Spinnen
description: The false leader of the de Spinnen family, actually Petrus, mundane son of Calvinus of Jerbiton and former mercenary, who serves as Florum's willing spokesman.

name: Arne de Spinnen
description: A childless former head of the de Spinnen family, himself not who he seemed, who accepted Petrus as his heir.

name: Valnastium
description: The Alpine home of House Jerbiton, where Petrus was born and where his children secretly trained as servants of the House.

name: Spinnen
description: A family descended from a maiden and the spider prince Spin Head, some of whom can weave cloth by touch; all are employed secretly by Florum.

name: Spin Head
description: The last and ugliest of the faerie princes, a spider who took human form, married the Spinnen ancestress and gave her the first flax plant as dowry.

name: Faerie Blood (Spinnen)
description: New Minor Virtue letting a character convert their body weight of fiber into cloth per day by touch, or unweave cloth.

name: Faerie Blood
description: A Virtue that Salvirius can grant to characters.

name: Strong Faerie Blood
description: A Virtue Salvirius can grant through a mystical quest.

name: Shapeshifter
description: A Virtue Salvirius can grant through a mystical quest.

name: Animal Ken
description: Listed among the Virtues/abilities Salvirius can grant.

name: Second Sight
description: A Virtue Salvirius can grant through a mystical quest.

name: Wilderness Sense
description: A Virtue Salvirius can grant through a mystical quest.

name: Pelagius
description: The person who discovered the Spinnen, when a dozen had the weaving ability.

name: Weavers' Guild of Ghent
description: The Ghent guild to which many Spinnen belong, hiding them in plain sight.

name: Ghent
description: Flemish city where Florum is located.

name: Spider's Palace
description: Vassal covenant of Florum at its original site, a faded faerie palace built by the spider prince, two days north of Ghent, with excellent laboratories.

name: Lotharingian Tribunal
description: A proposed new Tribunal to be carved from the western Rhine and adjacent Normandy, championed by Florum and Triamore.

name: House Guernicus
description: The House whose Quaesitores are scouting sites for a covenant should the Lotharingian Separation occur and who monitor Requies Aeterna.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House; a Tytalus hoplite visits Florum, and Normandy Tytali might recapture territory; home of the Cabal of Frankish Gold.

name: House Mercere
description: The Redcaps' House, which runs Mercer Houses in the Tribunal including at Cunfin and the Champagne fairs.

name: Rhesus of Verditus
description: Leader of Florum's magi, a weaver interested in the magical uses of flax, who came from the Roman Tribunal and supports the Lotharingian ideal.

name: House Verditius
description: Hermetic House of Rhesus, noted for professional jealousy among its members.

name: Roman Tribunal
description: Tribunal from which Rhesus came; Redcaps ply routes to it.

name: Calvinus of Jerbiton
description: A Florum magus with the Gentle Gift, posing as Piet's uncle, skilled in urban magic, illusions and spying; father of Petrus.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House of Calvinus, Eloi, Jerome and Norlanus, trained in urban magic.

name: Gentle Gift
description: Virtue possessed by Calvinus and all Cunfin magi except Angelus, easing dealings with mundanes.

name: Sophia
description: Calvinus' charming, bookish apprentice, posing as his daughter in Ghent.

name: Alroy of Flambeau
description: Florum's elderly Flambeau champion, a Levant veteran training an apprentice and seeking to rekindle his spirit.

name: House Flambeau
description: Martial Hermetic House; Flambeau and Tremere magi destroyed Bibracte.

name: Tourneying
description: Norman Hermetic contests over resources; Cunfin's hastiludium team has won three times in a row.

name: Prunellie of Merinita
description: An elderly Merinita maga studying the urban faeries of the Low Countries, allied with kabouters; she chose Florum's site.

name: House Merinita
description: Faerie-focused Hermetic House of Prunellie.

name: Kabouters
description: Dwarf-like faeries of the Low Countries who made bells for missionaries and sang the first carillon; Florum sits above their ancient workshop.

name: Faerie
description: Realm of Power; Faerie auras exist at Florum, Faux de Verzy, and the Blue Springs.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine realm; Low Countries faeries encouraged its spread; Clairvaux has Divine aura 6.

name: Magic
description: Realm of Power; Magic auras at Naours, Requies Aeterna, Mont Auxois and the Cunfin regio.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of Power; the Catalaunian Fields have a Malevolent Infernal aura 3 and an Infernal regio.

name: Aura
description: Supernatural strength of a Realm at a place, e.g. Faerie aura 4 at Faux de Verzy.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power harvested from sites such as destroyed faeries, the Grove of St. Lie and Catalaunian Fields.

name: Requies Aeterna
description: A small Winter covenant of Donatores at the ruins of Nesle, vassal of Florum, holding a noted library of Donatores lore.

name: Picardy
description: A relatively poor region bordering Flanders, Normandy, Ile de France and Champagne, under the influence of King Philip.

name: Flanders
description: Wealthy region bordering Picardy; its workers and woolens influence neighbors.

name: Forest of Cuise
description: A vast royal hunting forest south of Compiègne stretching to the Ardennes, with no known significant faerie presence.

name: Reims
description: Largest city in Picardy, seat of the most powerful French archbishopric and coronation site of French kings.

name: Philip II of France
description: The French king whose influence predominates in Picardy; met Richard the Lionheart at Vézelay.

name: Soissons
description: City in the Aisne valley, once capital of Syagrius' Roman kingdom and later Frankish capital.

name: Syagrius
description: Roman king of Soissons defeated by Clovis.

name: Clovis
description: Frankish king who defeated Syagrius and was baptized at Reims by St. Remigius.

name: Chlotar
description: Son of Clovis under whom Soissons was the Frankish capital.

name: Monastery of St. John of the Vines
description: Rich abbey in Soissons founded in the 11th century under royal patronage.

name: St. Remigius
description: Bishop of Reims who baptized Clovis; patron saint of Reims, born in Laon.

name: Holy Oil of Consecration
description: Phial of holy oil brought from heaven by a dove, a potent relic used to crown French kings.

name: William White Hands
description: Archbishop of Reims who granted the city a charter.

name: Porte de Mars
description: Roman triumphal gate at the north of Reims.

name: Monastery of St. Remigius
description: Eighth-century monastery and basilica over the grave of St. Remigius in Reims.

name: Notre-Dame de Reims
description: Vast cathedral in Reims begun in 1210 in the new French style.

name: Charlemagne's Talisman
description: Coronation relic in Reims believed to contain a fragment of the True Cross.

name: Reliquary of the Holy Thorn
description: Coronation relic kept in the archbishop's palace at Reims.

name: Montagne de Reims
description: Hilly forested limestone plateau south of Reims with chasms, wild beasts and vis sources.

name: Grove of St. Lie
description: Oak grove on a Gaulish burial mound with a chapel to St. Lie, whose flowers yield Creo vis as a tropaeum.

name: St. Lie
description: Fifth-century hermit-saint.

name: Tropaeum
description: Normandy legal category of vis source, such as the Grove of St. Lie.

name: Luctatio
description: Normandy legal category of contested vis source, such as the Cave of Sabinus.

name: Faux de Verzy
description: Sinister grove of twisted beeches with a Faerie aura of 4, where dark dwarf-like folk take villagers captive.

name: Miracle of Our Lady of Boulogne
description: Apparition of the Virgin in 636 leading to a crewless boat bearing her statue, now a pilgrim relic.

name: Nanteuil
description: Knights Templar priory in the Montagne de Reims, possibly a Divine regio.

name: Knights Templar
description: Military order with a priory at Nanteuil and a commandery at Laon.

name: Norlanus of Jerbiton
description: Elderly eremite Jerbiton magus at Laon's cathedral school holding a Terram vis legacy; wrote of Nanteuil as a regio.

name: Regio
description: A supernatural region layered on the mundane world, e.g. at Nanteuil, Cunfin and the Catalaunian Fields.

name: Twilight
description: Magical episodes affecting magi; Angelus sees it as seeing the Face of God; Eulogius nears Final Twilight.

name: Hautvillers Abbey
description: Abbey founded in 660 by St. Nivard, famed for decorated manuscripts.

name: St. Nivard
description: Founder of Hautvillers in 660.

name: Ay
description: Ancient Gaulish vintners' town with a royal residence.

name: Arras
description: Seat of Artois, with the Abbey of St. Vaast and a tradition of trouvères.

name: Abbey of St. Vaast
description: Benedictine abbey at Arras founded by St. Aubert housing St. Vaast's relics.

name: Gautier d'Arras
description: Famous 12th-century trouvère of Arras, author of Eracle.

name: Boulogne
description: Port and pilgrimage site where Claudius based his invasion of Britain.

name: Amiens
description: Historical capital of Picardy with relics of St. Martin's cloak and John the Baptist's head.

name: St. Martin of Tours
description: Saint whose cloak, halved for a beggar, is a relic of Amiens.

name: Blue Springs of the Somme
description: Enchanted pools with Faerie auras up to 3 inhabited by mischievous water sprites.

name: Water Sprites
description: Mischievous faeries of the Blue Springs that steal and waylay travelers.

name: Caves of Naours
description: Underground village with a Magic aura of 2, protected by a pact with a cave genius loci.

name: Genius Loci
description: A spirit of a place, such as those at Naours and the Cave of Sabinus.

name: Corbie
description: Benedictine abbey founded by St. Bathilde, major theological center where Carolingian script developed.

name: St. Bathilde
description: Wife of Clovis II and founder of Corbie.

name: St. Adalard
description: Cousin of Charlemagne under whom Corbie rose.

name: St. Ansgar
description: Apostle of the North born in Corbie, later archbishop of Hamburg.

name: Laon
description: Hilltop city, former Carolingian capital, with a famous cathedral school and where Norlanus lives.

name: Anselm of Laon
description: Scholar under whom Laon's cathedral school flourished.

name: Hugh Capet
description: Took Laon from the Carolingians and established his capital in Paris.

name: Charles the Bald
description: Carolingian king who endowed Laon and built the palace at Compiègne.

name: Compiègne
description: Ancient city on the Oise around a royal abbey of St. Cornelius.

name: Prémontré
description: Abbey in the Cuise Forest founded by St. Norbert, mother house of the Premonstratensians.

name: St. Norbert
description: Founder of the Premonstratensian order.

name: Premonstratensians
description: Severe order of preaching canons in white habits founded by St. Norbert.

name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
description: Great Cistercian churchman who founded Clairvaux and preached the Second Crusade at Vézelay.

name: Cistercian Order
description: Reforming austere monastic order with mother house at Cîteaux.

name: Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House of the Donatores, Angelus and Philip.

name: Donatores Requietis Aeternae
description: Ex Miscellanea tradition dedicated to helping the dead pass on and banishing the restless dead.

name: Nesle
description: Picard town ruined in the Donatores' battle against undead; site of Requies Aeterna.

name: Muirgheal
description: Quaesitor who arranged the Donatores' entry into the Order.

name: Restless Dead
description: Undead that plagued 11th-century France and were banished by the Donatores.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi.

name: Eulogius of House Ex Miscellanea
description: Decrepit founder of the Donatores who runs Requies Aeterna; a master of Perdo, Corpus and Mentem.

name: Henri
description: Youngest filius of Eulogius who preserves the Requies Aeterna library.

name: Perdo
description: Hermetic Technique mastered by Eulogius.

name: Corpus
description: Hermetic Form mastered by Eulogius.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Form mastered by Eulogius.

name: Creo
description: Hermetic Technique; Creo vis at the Grove of St. Lie.

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Form; Norlanus harvests Terram vis.

name: Aquam
description: Hermetic Form; Aquam vis at the Cave of Sabinus.

name: Wizard War
description: Hermetic legal feud; a plot seeks to use it against Eulogius.

name: Champagne
description: Rolling prosperous region famed for its trade fairs and Cistercian abbeys.

name: Cunfin
description: Covenant of magi and Cistercian monks in Champagne, a Mercer House with a Magic regio and Portal to Dragon's Rest.

name: Atramentum Renatus
description: Burgundian covenant of Helios, Gulo, Iacula and Philip founded after their ousting from Brittany.

name: Bibracte
description: Ruined Diedne covenant on Mont Beuvray that worshipped Vercingetorix, destroyed by Flambeau and Tremere.

name: Lixivia
description: Ruined, abandoned or lost covenant in Champagne and Burgundy.

name: Moles Magna
description: Ruined, abandoned or lost covenant in Champagne and Burgundy.

name: Châlons-en-Champagne
description: Ecclesiastical city on the Marne with Notre-Dame basilica and Notre-Dame-de-Vaux.

name: Provins
description: Champagne fair city with the Caesar Tower and court of Theobald IV.

name: Theobald IV of Champagne
description: 19-year-old poet Count of Champagne under his mother's regency.

name: Blanca of Navarre
description: Mother and regent of Theobald IV, loyal to King Philip.

name: Henry I of Champagne
description: Count under whom Provins and Troyes flourished.

name: Caesar Tower
description: Square watchtower and prison in Provins.

name: Champagne Trade Fairs
description: Six main fairs at Provins, Troyes, Lagny and Bar-sur-Aube where Redcaps run temporary Mercer Houses.

name: Mercer House
description: A Redcap trading and messaging post; Cunfin hosts the Tribunal's and temporary ones appear at fairs.

name: Confluensis
description: Powerful Normandy covenant, liege of Cunfin, which organizes Redcap trade.

name: Troyes
description: Champagne fair city with Jewish community, home of Chrétien de Troyes and Rashi.

name: St. Lupus
description: Early bishop who spared Troyes from Attila by offering himself as hostage.

name: Chrétien de Troyes
description: 12th-century poet of Arthurian romances including Perceval, the first work to mention the Grail.

name: Clairvaux Abbey
description: Major Cistercian abbey founded by St. Bernard in 1115 with a Divine aura of 6.

name: Rashi
description: Rabbi of Troyes famous for commentaries on the Tanakh and Talmud.

name: Rashi's Commentaries
description: Two great tractatus in Theology (Judaism), Quality 13.

name: Catalaunian Fields
description: Site of the 451 battle against Attila, with a Malevolent Infernal aura 3 and an Infernal regio yielding Perdo and Corpus vis.

name: Attila the Hun
description: Hun leader defeated at the Catalaunian Fields.

name: Merovech
description: Legendary sorcerer-king of the Franks at the Catalaunian Fields.

name: Aetius
description: Roman general at the Catalaunian Fields.

name: Theoderic
description: Visigoth king slain at the Catalaunian Fields.

name: Valoran
description: Student/filius of St. Nerius, rumored founder of Cunfin's monastery and believed parens of Angelus.

name: St. Nerius
description: Saint bridging Magic and Divine, followed by Eloi and Angelus.

name: Eloi of Jerbiton
description: Founder and prior of Cunfin, a pious Gentle Gifted magus bridging Order and Church.

name: Jerome of Jerbiton
description: Parens of Eloi at Confluensis who supported Cunfin's founding.

name: Celeres of Bonisagus
description: Ancient eccentric Bonisagus magus obsessed with the Grail, owner of the Grail Library.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Hermetic House of Celeres, Artorius and Iacula.

name: Holy Grail
description: Legendary holy vessel (or stone in Wolfram) sought by Celeres.

name: Mercere Portal
description: Magical portal; Cunfin houses one to Dragon's Rest.

name: Dragon's Rest
description: Destination of the Mercere Portal at Cunfin.

name: Holy Influence
description: Power Eloi uses to give Cunfin's Dominion a Calm temper.

name: Grail Library
description: Celeres' collection of texts on Arthur and the Grail at Cunfin.

name: Legends of Brittany
description: Summa on Faerie Lore by Celeres of Breton Arthurian tales.

name: Arthur Among the Britons
description: Tractatus on Area Lore: Britain by Celeres of Welsh Arthur tales.

name: The Llancarfan Saints' Lives
description: Tractatus, Dominion Lore, Quality 6, hagiographies referencing Arthur.

name: History of the Britons
description: Tractatus by Nennius, earliest account of Arthur.

name: History of the Kings of Britain
description: Tractatus by Geoffrey of Monmouth including the Prophecies of Merlin.

name: The Lais of Marie de France
description: Tractatus, Charm, by Marie de France.

name: Arthurian Romances
description: Tractatus, Etiquette, collection of Chrétien's four poems.

name: Perceval
description: Chrétien's unfinished tractatus on Dominion Lore, first to mention the Grail.

name: Joseph d'Arimethie
description: Tractatus by Robert de Boron on the Holy Grail.

name: Parsifal
description: Tractatus, Magic Lore, by Wolfram von Eschenbach placing the Grail at Munsalvaesche.

name: King Arthur
description: Legendary king of Britain central to the Arthurian cycle.

name: Merlin
description: Arthur's legendary wizard-adviser who vanished into Broceliande.

name: Nennius
description: Eighth-century British monk author of History of the Britons.

name: Geoffrey of Monmouth
description: Twelfth-century cleric author of History of the Kings of Britain.

name: Marie de France
description: Poet at the court of Marie of Champagne.

name: Robert de Boron
description: Author of Joseph d'Arimethie, first to call it the Holy Grail.

name: Wolfram von Eschenbach
description: German knight-poet author of Parsifal.

name: Munsalvaesche
description: Castle where Parsifal places the Grail, guarded by templeisen.

name: Grail Templars
description: Wolfram's Grail guardians, distinct from the Knights Templar.

name: Fisher King
description: Perceval's wounded host who guards the Grail.

name: Perceval (character)
description: Naive knight hero of Chrétien's romance who encounters the Grail.

name: Priory of St. Nerius
description: Group seeking recognition of St. Nerius, with whom Eloi has contact.

name: Dominican Order
description: Newly created order pursuing heretics, Eloi's current concern.

name: Angelus of Ex Miscellanea
description: Holy hermit co-founder of Cunfin who believes Twilight is seeing the Face of God.

name: Hervé filius Évrard
description: Redcap son of Évrard who runs the temporary Mercer House at the Champagne fairs.

name: Évrard de Tours
description: Senior Redcap of the Tribunal who relocated the Mercer House to Cunfin.

name: Renaud Fouinon
description: Redcap foundling, foster brother of Hervé and member of the Goliards.

name: Goliards
description: Group Renaud belongs to, hindering his advancement.

name: Artorius filius Celeres
description: Newly Gauntleted Bonisagus magus, Celeres' last apprentice.

name: Gauntlet
description: Rite ending apprenticeship, called 'knighting' by Celeres.

name: Longevity Ritual
description: Ritual Évrard began later in life.

name: Scales of the Magical Weight
description: InVi 5 effect in Hervé's enchanted devices.

name: Sense the Nature of Vis
description: InVi 5 effect in Hervé's enchanted devices.

name: Posing the Silent Question
description: InMe 20 effect in Hervé's enchanted devices.

name: Trust of the Childlike Faith
description: PeMe 10 effect in Hervé's enchanted devices.

name: Martin (abbot of Cunfin)
description: Middle-aged abbot of Cunfin who supports the magi.

name: Burgundy
description: Duchy in the southeast of the Tribunal, heartland of great monasteries.

name: Hugh IV of Burgundy
description: Eight-year-old Duke of Burgundy.

name: Alice de Vergy
description: Regent of Burgundy.

name: Cluny
description: Most powerful monastery, mother house of the Cluniacs.

name: Cîteaux
description: Mother house of the Cistercian order.

name: Vézelay
description: Benedictine monastery with relics of Mary Magdalene.

name: Auxerre
description: Holy city with the Abbey of St. Germanus.

name: St. Germanus
description: Fifth-century bishop of Auxerre.

name: Avallon
description: Walled hilltop town with a relic of St. Lazarus.

name: Gerard de Roussillon
description: Founder of Vézelay and bringer of St. Lazarus' relics to Autun.

name: The Morvan
description: Burgundian wilderness with contested vis sources and dark faeries.

name: Vercingetorix
description: Gallic chieftain worshipped by the Bibracte cult.

name: House Diedne
description: Former House whose magi founded Bibracte.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House that helped destroy Bibracte; Daria la Gris is Tremere.

name: Schism War
description: Hermetic war; Bibracte fell decades before it.

name: Mont Auxois
description: Site of Alesia with a Magic aura and haunted temple to Matres.

name: Matres
description: Gallic mother goddess with a temple at Alesia.

name: Fountain of St. Reina
description: Divine-aura curative fountain at Mont Auxois.

name: Autun
description: Great Roman city in Burgundy with the Cathedral of St. Lazarus.

name: Langres
description: Walled hilltop town of the Lingones.

name: Cave of Sabinus
description: Cave with a genius loci and Aquam vis, a luctatio.

name: Sabinus
description: Lingones chieftain who hid in the cave for nine years.

name: Dijon
description: Ducal capital of Burgundy.

name: Helios filius Kybella
description: Tytalus theurgist of Atramentum Renatus investigating Vercingetorix's spirit.

name: Gulo Midusulfis
description: Bjornaer co-founder of Atramentum Renatus.

name: House Bjornaer
description: Hermetic House of Gulo.

name: Iacula
description: Bonisagus maga researching projectile motion.

name: Philip of Ex Miscellanea
description: Donatores magus formerly of Requies Aeterna.

name: Fudarus
description: Breton covenant whose vassal Atramentum was taken over.

name: Exspectatio
description: Covenant formed when five Fudarus magi ousted Atramentum.

name: Code of Hermes
description: Hermetic law; also an Ability.

name: Peripheral Code
description: Tribunal-specific law.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Tribunal known for tradition, source of the Lotharingian movement.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: The Tribunal covered by this book.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: Order-wide meeting in 1228.

name: Novgorod Tribunal
description: Most recently created Tribunal, in 1008.

name: Provençal Tribunal
description: Tribunal that might welcome or fear the Lotharingian.

name: Greater Alps Tribunal
description: Tribunal sharing Arelat.

name: Triamore
description: Rhine covenant on the Ardennes, instigator of the Lotharingian Tribunal.

name: Daria la Gris
description: Tremere maga of Triamore.

name: Fengheld
description: Huge Rhine covenant partly supportive of Lotharingia.

name: Waddenzee
description: Martial pirate covenant on Terschelling.

name: Oculus Septentrionalis
description: Rhine covenant feuding with Waddenzee.

name: Cabal of Frankish Gold
description: Tytalan cabal supporting the Lotharingian Tribunal.

name: Augustina of Confluensis
description: Member of the Cabal of Frankish Gold.

name: Prima Buliste
description: Tytalus Prima, member of the cabal to distract a rival.

name: Trouvères
description: Noble knight-poets telling romances.

name: Jongleurs
description: Lower-born minstrels.

name: Chansons de geste
description: Great romances with arcane lore.

name: Free Expression
description: Virtue vital to trouvères.

name: Matter of Britain
description: Cycle of Arthurian tales.

name: Matter of France
description: Cycle of Charlemagne and paladins.

name: Gunnar Von Falster
description: Rhine magus rumored to have written Parsifal.

name: Montserrat
description: Mountain above Barcelona, possible Grail resting place.

name: Joan of Flanders
description: Commissioned Perceval continuations.

name: Durendal
description: Roland's legendary relic-hilted sword.

name: Roland
description: Charlemagne's paladin nephew killed at Roncevaux.

name: Salvirius
description: Mysterious scarred adviser of the Boar King who grants Virtues via quests.

name: Boar King
description: Faerie court ruler advised by Salvirius.

name: Charlemagne
description: Great king of the Matter of France.

name: Paladins
description: Charlemagne's twelve companions.

name: Theurgy
description: Helios is a Tytalan theurgist.
